3: **Source:** `docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md` §10.3, amendment P5-A (revised: hour cap removed).
4: **Branch:** `hardening`. One branch, one commit per verified step, commit mode ASK.
5: **Hour cap:** none. Work is ordered by dependency and gated by checks, not by a time budget.

10: ## 0. What this phase must achieve
11: 
12: 1. **Every known defect is closed or explicitly deferred with your approval.** Section 2 lists 32 defects. Each one has an owner step and a check. No defect is left "open" at phase close.
13: 2. **The app is safe with data.** A failed action never destroys a stored session or report. A crash never leaves two files out of step.
14: 3. **The verdict is correct.** Mate, illegal moves, timeouts, and partial engine results are handled and shown to the player, never silently dropped.
15: 4. **The first screen teaches the whole process.** A new player understands, before the camera opens, what the app does, what it never does, and what to do in order.
16: 5. **The flow is calm and recoverable.** One place says what state the app is in. Every screen has a clear next action, a clear way back, and no dead ends.
17: 6. **The UI meets a written standard.** Tokens, type scale, contrast, focus, keyboard, reduced motion, narrow and wide layouts, and plain copy. Each is checked, not assumed.
18: 7. **The backend is high quality.** Typed error codes, validated IPC, bounded work, cancellation, a file log with redaction, a `doctor` command, and tests where wrongness is silent.
19: 
20: **Honest limit.** No plan can prove a program has zero bugs. This phase does three things to get as close as possible: it names every known defect, it adds a bug bash with a written register, and it closes the phase only when no P0 or P1 defect is open. Behaviour that needs your camera, your SmartSpectra key, or a paid AI call is marked `NOT_RUN` until you run it. The agent does not claim it passed.

28: - **Paid calls need approval.** The real AI provider check (S59) uses a key and a spending limit you set.
29: - **Step order follows dependencies.** Workstream W1 (data safety) comes before anything that writes data. W5 (UI system) comes before W4 screens are polished, so new screens are built on tokens rather than retrofitted.
30: - **Every step has:** an outcome, files, tests written first, a check ID, and an acceptance line. Typecheck and `npm test` pass before a commit.
31: - **Documentation.** Each step adds to `docs/decisions.md` if it makes a choice. The bug register is `docs/phases/phase-05-bugs.md`, updated in the same commit as each fix.

78: ## 3. Experience design
79: 
80: ### 3.1 The flow
81: 
82: One set of screens, owned by one state machine (S46). The state names are what the player sees in the header.
83: 
84: ```
85: Home ──► Setup ──► Sensing ──► Stopped ──► Games (paste) ──► Review (report)
86:  │         │          │           │                              │
87:  │         └──────────┴───────────┴──────── back to Home ◄───────┘
88:  └──► Sessions list ──► Review of an earlier session
89: ```
90: 
91: - **Home.** The first screen. Shows the process explainer the first time, then a plain list of recent sessions and one primary action: **Start a session**.
92: - **Setup.** Four checks in order: privacy and consent, SmartSpectra key present, camera framing, and time control. Start stays disabled until the first three pass, and each disabled reason is written next to the control.
93: - **Sensing.** A persistent recording indicator, the live pulse strip, elapsed time, the between-games marker, a quality reading, and the Stop control. Stop asks for confirmation.
94: - **Stopped.** A summary: duration, baseline, coverage, and what to do next. The next step is pasting games.
95: - **Games.** Paste PGNs oldest first. Each game shows its own state, and an illegal move points to its exact move number.
96: - **Review.** The verdict, the timeline, the bands, the games, and the optional AI reading. A refusal shows the real reason and the remedy.
97: 
98: ### 3.2 The first screen: "How ChessPulse works"
99: 
100: Shown the first time the app opens, reopenable from **Help**, and never shown again once dismissed (preference stored locally). It is not a wall of text: five numbered steps with one line each and a visible "You are here" marker as the player moves through setup.
101: 
102: Proposed copy. Final wording is a S47 deliverable and goes through the copy pass (S56).
103: 
104: > **ChessPulse reviews your chess session after you play.**
105: >
106: > It watches your pulse through the camera while you play on chess.com, then shows your pulse next to your moves, so you can see whether a bad stretch lined up with a stressful stretch.
107: >
108: > **How it works**
109: >
110: > 1. **Allow the camera.** Nothing is recorded. No video or image is saved. Only pulse numbers are stored, on this computer.
111: > 2. **Check your framing.** Sit so your upper chest is in view and you are the only face on screen.
112: > 3. **Play on chess.com.** ChessPulse does not show anything during a game. Mark each game end with one button.
113: > 4. **Stop and paste your games.** Copy the PGNs from chess.com, oldest first.
114: > 5. **Read your review.** One verdict line, one timeline, and the accuracy in calm and elevated pulse periods.
115: >
116: > **What ChessPulse never does**
117: >
118: > - It does not give advice during a rated game.
119: > - It does not diagnose anything or give medical advice.
120: > - It does not upload your data. Everything stays local.
121: >
122: > [Start setup]  [Skip for now]
123: 
124: Design rules for this screen:
125: 
126: - It states limits ("never does") as plainly as features.
127: - The fair-play line appears here, in the README, and in the review footer.
128: - The step list is also the setup progress, so the player sees the same order later.
129: 
130: ### 3.3 Setup and framing (S48)
131: 
132: - A live preview with a framing guide: a face outline, a chest line, and three checks (one face, chest visible, enough light). Each check turns green, and the text says what to do ("Move back until your chest is in the frame"). The text comes from validation hints the SDK already sends.
133: - Consent is one clear action, with the same wording as the README.
134: - If the SDK key is missing, Setup says so in one sentence with the name of the variable to set, and nothing else. The key value is never shown.
135: - The player can start only when all three checks are green. A "Start anyway" option does not exist, because a session below the coverage gate produces only a refusal.
136: 
137: ### 3.4 Sensing (S49)
138: 
139: - A recording indicator with a red dot and the word "Sensing" stays visible on every screen while the camera is open, not only on this one.
140: - Elapsed time, and a warning at 80 minutes that the session stops at 90.
141: - The between-games control has two clear states: "Game ended — waiting for next game" and "Playing". It shows how many games have been marked.
142: - A quality reading ("Good signal", "Weak signal, check lighting") from the usable-sample ratio over the last minute.
143: - Stop asks "Stop this session? You can't add to it later." with Stop and Keep sensing.
144: 
145: ### 3.5 Errors and empty states
146: 
147: Every error has three parts: what happened, why, and the next action. Examples the copy pass must cover:
148: 
149: - No key → "SmartSpectra key not found. Add `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY` to `.env`, then restart."
150: - Camera refused → "ChessPulse cannot open the camera. Check that another app is not using it, then try again."
151: - Illegal move → "Game 2, move 23 (Nf6) is not legal from this position. Check that the PGN came from chess.com."
152: - Low coverage → the existing remedy, reworded to name the one thing to change first.
153: - Empty sessions list → "No sessions yet. Start one from Home."
154: 
155: ### 3.6 Visual standard (W5)
156: 
157: - One token file: colour roles (surface, text, muted, accent, warn, danger, focus), a type scale, a 4 px spacing grid, radii, and motion durations.
158: - Accent colour means one thing only (the measured pulse line, per the S21 checkpoint).
159: - Every text/background pair in the app meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI graphics). A script checks the pairs.
160: - Elevated periods carry a shape or label, not colour alone.
161: - Reduced motion removes the strip's animation and the recording pulse.
162: - Layouts checked at 960, 1100, 1440 px wide and at a narrow phone-sized width.
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## 4. Steps
167: 
168: Each step lists its check IDs. Check definitions are in section 5.
169: 
170: ### Workstream W1 — Data safety
171: 
172: **S29 — Keep the previous report on a failed or refused build (BUG-01, BUG-02).**
173: - Decision: a failed or refused build keeps the previous report. The old report and old games stay together. Recorded in `decisions.md`.
174: - Change: remove the early `deleteReport` from `buildReport`. Write `games.json` and `report.json` only after the report object is valid. Add `gamesDigest` (SHA-256 of the PGN batch) to `reportSchema`. Missing digest on an old report counts as stale.
175: - The AI path (`insight-ipc.ts`, `ai/service.ts`) recomputes the digest before any provider call. A mismatch returns a message asking the player to rebuild, with no provider call.
176: - Tests: failed PGN keeps report bytes; low-coverage refusal keeps old report; successful rebuild replaces both files with matching digests; hand-edited `games.json` blocks the AI call (injected `fetch` must not be called).
177: - Checks: H-01.
178: 
179: **S30 — Atomic multi-file writes and safe temp files (BUG-02, BUG-24).**
180: - `writeAtomic` uses a random suffix per write, closes the handle exactly once, and syncs the directory after rename so the rename survives a crash.
181: - A two-file save writes both temp files, renames `games.json`, then renames `report.json`. A crash between renames leaves a digest mismatch, which S29 already refuses.
182: - Tests: forced failure after the temp write removes the temp file; a double-close path cannot throw; the directory sync is called (through an injected fs seam).
183: - Checks: H-02.
184: 
185: **S31 — Storage failure and the time limit end the session once, with a reason (BUG-05, BUG-06).**
186: - New event `cp:session:ended` with `reason: 'storage' | 'limit'` and a player-facing message. Stop reasons `storage` and `limit` added to the header schema. Existing headers still parse.
187: - Capture gets an `onEnded` callback. A failed flush calls it instead of a bare `shutdown()`.
188: - The 90-minute limit is a timer armed at session start, not a check on incoming batches. A session with no samples still ends at the limit.
189: - `stopEverything` remains the single finalizer, so the event cannot finalize twice.
190: - Tests: session test for the limit timer's stored reason; contract test for the new event; fake-SDK test that a failing write produces exactly one `onEnded('storage')`.
191: - Manual (NOT_RUN until S59): force a write failure with a read-only session folder during a short real run.
192: - Checks: H-03.
193: 
194: **S32 — Clean shutdown and crash recovery (regression coverage).**
195: - A test kills the process mid-sensing (child process, forced exit) and confirms the next start recovers the session with a `crash` reason and a coverage value.
196: - Window close, quit, and consent revocation all drain the last batch before the header closes. Each has a test using the fake SDK.
197: - Checks: H-04.
198: 
199: ### Workstream W2 — Analysis correctness
200: 
201: **S33 — Mate-aware scoring and terminal positions (BUG-03, BUG-04).**
202: - Decision: a mate score maps to `sign(N) × (10000 − 100·|N|)`. Mate in 1 is +9900. Terminal positions (checkmate, stalemate) are detected with `chess.js` and never sent to the engine.
203: - `MoveMetric` and `TimelineMove` gain `mate: boolean`. A mate-involved move shows `cpl: null` in the display (the 9900 value would dominate CPL ticks) but counts in blunders and accuracy.
204: - Tests: a move from +50 into a position where the opponent mates is a blunder with `mate: true`; a mating move is not a blunder, accuracy 100, and the engine is not called (counting fake engine); a move into stalemate from a won position is a blunder; mate values are monotonic (mate in 1 > mate in 2 > +1000 > 0). Fixture FENs: `6k1/5ppp/8/8/8/8/8/R5K1 w` and `R5k1/5ppp/8/8/8/8/8/6K1 b`.
205: - Checks: H-05.
206: 
207: **S34 — Illegal moves are found at paste time and named (BUG-07).**
208: - Paste validation replays every game (`positionsFromMoves`). The first illegal move gets a per-game message with the move number and SAN.
209: - The report builder refuses a batch with any illegal move. It no longer truncates a game silently.
210: - Tests: an illegal move at move 23 is reported as game N, move 23; a legal game passes; a batch with an illegal game refuses the whole report, not one game.
211: - Checks: H-06.
212: 
213: **S35 — Engine robustness and a visible progress path (BUG-13, BUG-14, BUG-15).**
214: - Each position has a timeout and a retry on worker crash, with a bounded number of worker restarts per report.
215: - The report build reports progress ("Scored 34 of 80 positions") through a progress event, and supports cancel. Cancel terminates the worker and leaves the previous report intact (S29).
216: - A position that still fails is counted, and the Review screen states how many positions were not scored and why ("3 positions timed out and were left out").
217: - Tests: a fake worker that never answers times out and is counted; a crashed worker restarts once and the build continues; cancel leaves the old report bytes intact.
218: - Checks: H-07.
219: 
220: **S36 — Engine depth measured, decision recorded.**
221: - `scripts/engine-depth-bench.mjs` runs every position in the fixture games at depths 6, 8, and 12. It prints mean and p95 time, total time, and the count of blunder flags that change between depths.
222: - Rule decided before the run: raise to 12 only if mean time is at most 400 ms per position on this machine and at most 5% of blunder flags change. Otherwise keep 8.
223: - Limit: fixtures measure speed and stability, not accuracy. Accuracy calibration needs real games and stays open, and the review page says so in the engine note.
224: - Checks: H-08.
225: 
226: **S37 — Linear-time analysis paths (BUG-21, BUG-22).**
227: - `bandAt` uses a sorted array with binary search. `moveTimes` becomes a `Map` keyed by game and move.
228: - Tests: results equal the old implementation on the fixtures (keep the old function in the test as the oracle); a 90-minute synthetic session builds a report in under a stated time on this machine, recorded in the phase note.
229: - Checks: H-09.
230: 
231: **S38 — AI grounding: numbers and claims (BUG-25, BUG-26).**
232: - The validator adds a claims check. It rejects diagnostic or medical terms and claims about the player's mental or physical state (a fixed list, tested with adversarial fixtures in `tests/fixtures/ai/`).
233: - Before the request shape is finalized, check the current provider docs for each preset (AGENTS §8: read live docs, not memory). Record the checked date and the exact field names in `decisions.md`.
234: - A reply with `content: null` and a reasoning field is an explicit error, not a silent "unreadable response", so the player sees what happened.
235: - Checks: H-10.
236:

170: ### Workstream W1 — Data safety
171: 
172: **S29 — Keep the previous report on a failed or refused build (BUG-01, BUG-02).**
173: - Decision: a failed or refused build keeps the previous report. The old report and old games stay together. Recorded in `decisions.md`.
174: - Change: remove the early `deleteReport` from `buildReport`. Write `games.json` and `report.json` only after the report object is valid. Add `gamesDigest` (SHA-256 of the PGN batch) to `reportSchema`. Missing digest on an old report counts as stale.
175: - The AI path (`insight-ipc.ts`, `ai/service.ts`) recomputes the digest before any provider call. A mismatch returns a message asking the player to rebuild, with no provider call.
176: - Tests: failed PGN keeps report bytes; low-coverage refusal keeps old report; successful rebuild replaces both files with matching digests; hand-edited `games.json` blocks the AI call (injected `fetch` must not be called).
177: - Checks: H-01.
178: 
179: **S30 — Atomic multi-file writes and safe temp files (BUG-02, BUG-24).**
180: - `writeAtomic` uses a random suffix per write, closes the handle exactly once, and syncs the directory after rename so the rename survives a crash.
181: - A two-file save writes both temp files, renames `games.json`, then renames `report.json`. A crash between renames leaves a digest mismatch, which S29 already refuses.
182: - Tests: forced failure after the temp write removes the temp file; a double-close path cannot throw; the directory sync is called (through an injected fs seam).
183: - Checks: H-02.
184: 
185: **S31 — Storage failure and the time limit end the session once, with a reason (BUG-05, BUG-06).**
186: - New event `cp:session:ended` with `reason: 'storage' | 'limit'` and a player-facing message. Stop reasons `storage` and `limit` added to the header schema. Existing headers still parse.
187: - Capture gets an `onEnded` callback. A failed flush calls it instead of a bare `shutdown()`.
188: - The 90-minute limit is a timer armed at session start, not a check on incoming batches. A session with no samples still ends at the limit.
189: - `stopEverything` remains the single finalizer, so the event cannot finalize twice.
190: - Tests: session test for the limit timer's stored reason; contract test for the new event; fake-SDK test that a failing write produces exactly one `onEnded('storage')`.
191: - Manual (NOT_RUN until S59): force a write failure with a read-only session folder during a short real run.
192: - Checks: H-03.
193: 
194: **S32 — Clean shutdown and crash recovery (regression coverage).**
195: - A test kills the process mid-sensing (child process, forced exit) and confirms the next start recovers the session with a `crash` reason and a coverage value.
196: - Window close, quit, and consent revocation all drain the last batch before the header closes. Each has a test using the fake SDK.

199: ### Workstream W2 — Analysis correctness
200: 
201: **S33 — Mate-aware scoring and terminal positions (BUG-03, BUG-04).**
202: - Decision: a mate score maps to `sign(N) × (10000 − 100·|N|)`. Mate in 1 is +9900. Terminal positions (checkmate, stalemate) are detected with `chess.js` and never sent to the engine.
203: - `MoveMetric` and `TimelineMove` gain `mate: boolean`. A mate-involved move shows `cpl: null` in the display (the 9900 value would dominate CPL ticks) but counts in blunders and accuracy.
204: - Tests: a move from +50 into a position where the opponent mates is a blunder with `mate: true`; a mating move is not a blunder, accuracy 100, and the engine is not called (counting fake engine); a move into stalemate from a won position is a blunder; mate values are monotonic (mate in 1 > mate in 2 > +1000 > 0). Fixture FENs: `6k1/5ppp/8/8/8/8/8/R5K1 w` and `R5k1/5ppp/8/8/8/8/8/6K1 b`.
205: - Checks: H-05.
206: 
207: **S34 — Illegal moves are found at paste time and named (BUG-07).**
208: - Paste validation replays every game (`positionsFromMoves`). The first illegal move gets a per-game message with the move number and SAN.
209: - The report builder refuses a batch with any illegal move. It no longer truncates a game silently.
210: - Tests: an illegal move at move 23 is reported as game N, move 23; a legal game passes; a batch with an illegal game refuses the whole report, not one game.
211: - Checks: H-06.
212: 
213: **S35 — Engine robustness and a visible progress path (BUG-13, BUG-14, BUG-15).**
214: - Each position has a timeout and a retry on worker crash, with a bounded number of worker restarts per report.
215: - The report build reports progress ("Scored 34 of 80 positions") through a progress event, and supports cancel. Cancel terminates the worker and leaves the previous report intact (S29).
216: - A position that still fails is counted, and the Review screen states how many positions were not scored and why ("3 positions timed out and were left out").
217: - Tests: a fake worker that never answers times out and is counted; a crashed worker restarts once and the build continues; cancel leaves the old report bytes intact.
218: - Checks: H-07.
219: 
220: **S36 — Engine depth measured, decision recorded.**
221: - `scripts/engine-depth-bench.mjs` runs every position in the fixture games at depths 6, 8, and 12. It prints mean and p95 time, total time, and the count of blunder flags that change between depths.
222: - Rule decided before the run: raise to 12 only if mean time is at most 400 ms per position on this machine and at most 5% of blunder flags change. Otherwise keep 8.
223: - Limit: fixtures measure speed and stability, not accuracy. Accuracy calibration needs real games and stays open, and the review page says so in the engine note.
224: - Checks: H-08.
225: 
226: **S37 — Linear-time analysis paths (BUG-21, BUG-22).**
227: - `bandAt` uses a sorted array with binary search. `moveTimes` becomes a `Map` keyed by game and move.
228: - Tests: results equal the old implementation on the fixtures (keep the old function in the test as the oracle); a 90-minute synthetic session builds a report in under a stated time on this machine, recorded in the phase note.
229: - Checks: H-09.

231: **S38 — AI grounding: numbers and claims (BUG-25, BUG-26).**

235: - Checks: H-10.

237: **S39 — Coach memory and latency (BUG-23).**
238: - The coach keeps a rolling window of samples (the last ten minutes plus the baseline minute) and computes the baseline once, when the first minute completes.
239: - Tests: the baseline is computed once; memory stays bounded across a long synthetic session; a gap change clears the latch exactly as before.

244: **S40 — Typed error model (BUG-27).**

Each code has one player-facing message in one file.

267: - Session delete: removes the folder after a confirmation in the UI, and the index is rewritten atomically.
